How would you rate your competence in deciding which tool or method best fits the task at hand?
How would you rate your understanding of accessibility standards and legal requirements for digital content, and what they mean in practice?
How would you rate your competence in creating and checking digital content so it meets accessibility standards and works for people with different needs?
How would you rate your competence in supporting good accessibility practice beyond your own work - whether by modelling it, helping colleagues or flagging where standards aren't being met?
How would you rate your competence in checking that the information you work with and share is accurate, current and from a reliable source?
How would you rate your competence in organising, classifying and managing information and files so they are easy to find, appropriately protected and correctly disposed of when no longer needed?
How would you rate your understanding of user-centred principles and why understanding user needs matters for the work you do?
How would you rate your competence in finding out what users need - and using that insight to improve your work or processes?
How would you rate your ability to keep user needs in view when other priorities or pressures are pulling in a different direction?

question: How would you rate your understanding of how digital, data and AI can transform the way teams work and deliver outcomes?
How would you rate your competence in encouraging and supporting colleagues to adopt digital, data and AI approaches in your work?
How would you rate your competence in helping colleagues feel confident about digital change - including when they are uncertain or sceptical?
How would you rate your understanding of data and its role in decision-making?
How would you rate your competence in using data in your day-to-day work?
How would you rate your competence in using the data tools and systems relevant to your role?
How would you rate your competence in drawing on data rather than instinct or assumption when you need to make a decision?
How would you rate your competence in making sure the data you work with and share is handled safely and responsibly?
How would you rate your competence in evaluating and improving the data processes you work with?
How would you rate your competence in questioning the data you use - for example, where it came from, how it was collected, or whether it tells the full story?
How would you rate your understanding of visual data - including how charts and tables work, and how visual formats can help or mislead?
How would you rate your competence in reading and extracting meaning from charts and tables?
How would you rate your competence in creating clear and effective visualisations?
How would you rate your competence in considering whether the visual data you create or share works for people with different needs, including those using assistive technologies?
How would you rate your understanding of how data moves through its lifecycle from collection to disposal - including what happens at each stage and why responsible handling throughout matters?
How would you rate your competence in collecting and recording data correctly?
How would you rate your competence in storing and sharing data securely?
How would you rate your competence in disposing of data correctly?
How would you rate your competence in making sure data is handled consistently and responsibly when it crosses team or organisational boundaries?
How would you rate your understanding of data quality and why it matters for decisions and outcomes?
How would you rate your competence in identifying, correcting and cleaning data to ensure it is accurate and complete?
How would you rate your competence in assessing whether data are representative and unbiased?
How would you rate your understanding of the legal and ethical framework governing how data should be collected, used and shared?
How would you rate your competence in checking that data you access, use or share is handled lawfully and ethically?
How would you rate your competence in identifying and responding to legal and ethical risks or violations in how data is used?
How would you rate your understanding of data standards and why consistency and interoperability matter across government?
How would you rate your competence in applying agreed data standards in your own work and flagging when data doesn't meet them?
How would you rate your understanding of data analysis and how it supports decision-making - including what kinds of questions it can answer and what its limitations are?
How would you rate your competence in using analytical tools and software to work with data?
How would you rate your competence in working out what question you need to answer and finding the right data to answer it?
How would you rate your competence in communicating analytical findings, including uncertainty and limitations?
How would you rate your understanding of data sharing across teams and organisations, including what enables it and what governs it?
How would you rate your competence in sharing data with other teams and organisations safely, lawfully and effectively?
How would you rate your competence in finding, accessing and reusing data that others have shared?
How would you rate your competence in working with others to make data sharing across your organisation easier and more consistent?
How would you rate your understanding of how people respond to uncertainty and change at work, and why that affects whether innovation happens?
How would you rate your competence in identifying what it takes to get a new idea off the ground - who needs convincing, what concerns to address, and how to frame the proposal?
How would you rate your effectiveness in making it feel safe for colleagues to share ideas, try new things and admit when things go wrong?
How would you rate your effectiveness in responding when an experiment or new idea doesn't work out - in your own work and when it happens to colleagues?
How would you rate your competence in coping with change at work and supporting colleagues who are finding it hard?
How would you rate your understanding of where innovation is most likely to make a real difference - and what makes something a genuine opportunity rather than change for its own sake?
How would you rate your competence in using evidence to identify where innovation or improvement is most needed - and assess whether an opportunity is realistic and worth pursuing?
How would you rate how consistently you think about what users actually experience when deciding where innovation or improvement is most needed?
How would you rate your competence in constructively challenging established ways of working when you think something could be done better?
How would you rate your competence in seeking out connections between your work and what's happening elsewhere - in other teams, disciplines or sectors - to inform where and how you innovate?
How would you rate your understanding of the stages of the innovation lifecycle, from identifying a problem through to testing, refining and deciding whether to stop or scale a solution?

How would you rate your understanding of what makes a test or prototype genuinely useful, such as a minimum viable product designed to test critical assumptions, before committing to a solution fully?
How would you rate your competence in trying out new ideas on a small scale first - learning from what happens before committing to them fully?
How would you rate how consistently you reflect on what worked and what didn't when you try something new or test an idea - and share what you found with others who might benefit?
How would you rate your understanding of how to communicate an idea for change in a way that genuinely persuades different audiences?
How would you rate your competence in tailoring your communication of ideas for change to different audiences, framing them in ways that connect to outcomes people genuinely care about?
How would you rate your understanding of structured approaches to continuous improvement - the principles, methods and tools that help teams regularly review and improve how they work?
How would you rate your competence in implementing improvements deliberately and measuring whether they have had the effect you intended - rather than making changes and hoping for the best?
How would you rate how consistently you treat improvement as an ongoing habit - regularly reviewing how work is going and keeping that focus alive in your team even when other pressures mount?
How would you rate your understanding of what makes it hard to spread a successful idea or new way of working more widely - and what helps overcome those challenges?

How would you rate your competence in actively supporting the adoption of new approaches - at whatever level your role allows, from helping a colleague understand a change to planning how it reaches different teams?
How would you rate your competence in supporting and championing change to help maintain momentum - even when the initial excitement fades?

How would you rate your competence in actively connecting with colleagues in other teams, departments or organisations - sharing what has worked and helping proven approaches reach people who could benefit from them?
How would you rate your understanding of what AI is, how it works and what it can and cannot do?
How would you rate your competence in using AI tools in your everyday work?
How would you rate your competence in specifying and preparing inputs so AI systems produce reliable, useful outputs?
How would you rate your competence in checking whether an AI output is reliable before acting on it or sharing it with others?
How would you rate your understanding of where AI and automation can and cannot add value - including what kinds of tasks AI tends to help with and what makes some tasks unsuitable?
How would you rate your competence in identifying tasks, inefficiencies or pain points that AI could help address?
How would you rate your competence in weighing up whether AI is the right solution for a problem, taking into account its limitations and risks alongside its potential benefits?
How would you rate your understanding of your organisation's rules on which AI tools are approved for use and what data can safely be shared with them?

How would you rate your competence in spotting when a specific AI prompt or task carries a safety risk - whether from the data it contains or from the nature of the task itself - and adjusting or stopping before proceeding?
How would you rate your ability to escalate concerns about AI use to the right person when something feels wrong?
How would you rate your understanding of how AI generates outputs and why they may be unreliable or biased?
How would you rate your competence in checking and interpreting AI outputs before acting on them?
How would you rate your competence in making clear to others when a decision or recommendation has been informed by AI - including what that means for how certain you are?
How would you rate your competence in deciding when to trust an AI output and when to question or override it?
How would you rate your understanding of the legal and regulatory frameworks that govern AI use?
How would you rate your competence in applying governance and compliance requirements when using or commissioning AI?
How would you rate your competence in identifying and responding to governance and compliance risks in AI use?
How would you rate your understanding of the ethical principles that should guide responsible AI use in public services?
How would you rate your competence in applying fairness and public benefit considerations when using or recommending AI?
How would you rate your competence in making AI use transparent and explainable to those affected by it?
How would you rate your ability to consider the wider and longer-term effects of using AI - including on people who won't be in the room when decisions are made?
How would you rate your ability to factor in the environmental cost of AI when deciding whether and how to use it?
